OzyVTT · polish · consistency sweep 5

Fifth sweep

Asked for twenty-four, after sixteen last time. The mockups as the fourth sweep left them, every page at laptop and phone size, in Dusk and in Dawn: 127 pages and 5,490 captures, each measured from its computed style. To the earlier parts it adds tags, faces, closes, tabs, fields, lamps, cards, keyboard hints, text that is clipped, spills or wraps, and the contrast of every line against what is behind it. The owner asked for all twenty-five fixes, and each is now made in the approved mockups and their specs (T-consistency/SPEC.md section 8, ADR-0076). Each finding shows its parts before and after, from the approved mockups as they were and as they are now. Press a picture or its toggle to flip it; the after state has an amber frame. On a phone a wide picture keeps its size and scrolls sideways.

12345678910111213141516171819202122232425SwitchesGM ONLYOverlaysDanger

What doesn't match

Twenty-five differences, most to least visible, each seen in a picture or confirmed in the computed styles. One is a broken phone page (1) and one a colour fault in Dawn (2); the rest are parts drawn more than one way. All twenty-five are fixed; section 8.4 of the spec notes where a fix reaches less than the finding listed.

Every picture
1

The table screen's menu page draws a laptop bar on a phone

H, table screen (In the menu, The preview; phone)

On a phone a section's page stacks its header and its strip (rule 12). Behind the menu and the docked preview, the table screen's phone pages draw the laptop's section bar under the header: PREP a second time, its tabs, and its search, whose placeholder runs over the tabs.

Fix: The phone's strip of Prep's pages under the header, as Prep's own phone pages draw it.

The captures beside their pattern

2

Amber, magenta and violet words fail contrast in Dawn

Every area, in Dawn

A line of text needs 4.5:1 against what is behind it. In Dawn, amber words (Wait, Waiting, Your turn, 6 tokens in the tray) reach 2.3:1 in 38 places, magenta words (HOMEBREW, 1 homebrew, the stat block's Actions) 2.7:1 in 15, and violet words (GM ONLY, Hidden, TO LYRA, the GM's mark) 3.6:1 in 60. Dawn already has its own shades for danger text and cyan words; amber, magenta and violet use one colour for a word, a lamp and a line.

Fix: Dawn gets text shades for the three, at 5:1 or better (amber #875400, magenta #a3246b, violet #6a44bf), and words in those meanings use them; lamps, edges and fills keep their colours.

The captures beside their pattern

3

The Compendium's kind cards are drawn their own way on a laptop

G, the Compendium (Home, laptop); F, the Codex (Home)

A kind of thing with its count is a card on the Codex home and on the Compendium home on a phone: its icon and name, the count in VT323 30 px under them, its line. On a laptop the Compendium draws its own: the icon in a 42 px cyan box, the name at 15 px and the count at the right at 32 px.

Fix: One kind card, as the Codex draws it; the Compendium keeps its line of examples under the count.

The captures beside their pattern

4

The frame's turn order is drawn its own way

A, the frame (its sample of the table); C, the table

The frame's sample of the table draws the turn order with 28 px faces on a 1 px rim and gives Goblin 2 "G", the Goblin Boss "B" and Borin "O". The table draws 38 px faces on a 2 px rim with G2, GB and B, as every other piece does.

Fix: The table's faces and initials in the frame's turn order.

The captures beside their pattern

5

The stat block repeats the record's name

G, the Compendium (a monster's record)

A record opens with its title (T 2.2, rule 12). The Compendium's record shows GOBLIN BOSS as its title and again as the stat block's own head right under it, the stat block's larger on a laptop (22 px beside 21).

Fix: Inside its record the stat block starts with its line; it keeps its name where it stands alone, as in C3's monster picker.

The captures beside their pattern

6

Two bars are full boxes with a fill

F, the Codex (Home, the date bar); G, the Compendium (Home, Sources)

A group you act in is a Cradle: no fill, a 2 px base, sides that fade before the top (T 2.4). The Codex's date bar (Publish, Edit calendar) and the Compendium's Sources line (Import a pack, Export) are 1 px boxes on all four sides with a fill.

Fix: Both as the Cradle.

The captures beside their pattern

7

A read-only group is drawn as a box

F, the Codex (Home, laptop)

A group you only read is open, its heading in the eyebrow and a rule between groups (T 2.3). The Codex home draws Recently changed, a list of links, as a Cradle, while Where the party is and Reveal check beside it are open.

Fix: Recently changed open, as its neighbours are.

A harmful condition in two type styles

C, C2, C3, C4 and C6, C5 (Prone); D, characters (Poisoned)

Prone on the table's turn order is Bai Jamjuree at 10.5 px in an 18 px box; Poisoned on the roster is a VT323 16 px tag in a 22 px box.

Fix: One condition tag: VT323 16 px in its 22 px box, in --danger-text.

The captures beside their pattern

9

Sheet and dialog closes are drawn three ways

C3, running; C5; D, characters; E2, E3, F, G, I

C3's sheets and D's dialogs close with a plain 19 px icon (44 and 40 px). Prep's, the Codex's, the Compendium's and Settings' dialogs close with a 15 px icon on a Base line (36 px, 44 on a phone). The dice options close with the word Done on a laptop and the icon on a phone. The third sweep kept overlay heads' icons plain (SPEC 6.6).

Fix: One close: a plain icon at 18 px, 40 px on a laptop and 44 px on a phone, as A's dialog draws it; the dice options close with it too.

The captures beside their pattern

10

The Dusk and Dawn switch is drawn three ways

B, arrival; A's menu (and H's); I, settings (Device)

Arrival draws it as 32 px options on a glass plate, A's menu as 32 px segments and Settings as 36 px segments. A segment on a laptop is 36 px (T 2.5).

Fix: 36 px segments on their base lines everywhere; arrival keeps its plate over the art.

The captures beside their pattern

11

Steppers at two heights, their numbers at three sizes

C2, C4 and C6, C5 (32 px); G, I (40 px)

The dice options' stepper is 32 px with its number in VT323 19 px. The Compendium's editor and Settings draw theirs at 40 px with 24 and 22 px numbers, and the Compendium writes its minus as a hyphen.

Fix: One stepper: 40 px (44 px on a phone), its number VT323 22 px, the minus sign.

The captures beside their pattern

12

Boxed words in Bai Jamjuree beside the VT323 tag

B, arrival; I, its leftovers; F, time and tools

A state is a boxed tag in VT323 capitals (rule 19). Arrival's CLAIMED and the API reference's GET and POST are boxed Bai Jamjuree at 10.5 px. A template's parts (Checklist, Text, Strong start, Rooms) are boxed Bai Jamjuree chips at 11 px, though they are kinds and names, not states.

Fix: CLAIMED, GET and POST as VT323 tags; a template's parts as their icon and word with no box, as rule 19 draws a kind.

A hashtag drawn two ways

F, time and tools (a record); F, finding and pages (the index)

The pages index draws #thornwick as a Base line chip with its count; a record in time and tools draws it as a boxed 19 px tag.

Fix: The pages index's chip wherever a hashtag appears.

14

A record's or a pane's title at 17 to 22 px

E3, F, F3, G, I's leftovers (phones); F, G (laptops)

A title row is 24 px on a laptop and 20 px on a phone (T 2.2). A title that opens a record or a pane inside the page varies: on a phone 17 px (the Compendium's editor), 18 (writing a page, a replay), 19 (a Compendium record, a template, the calendar), 20, 21 (a Codex page) and 22 (an operation, a pin); on a laptop 21 (a Compendium record, a search result) and 22.

Fix: 22 px on a laptop and 20 px on a phone.

D, characters (Making, Level up); E, prep; G, the Compendium

One Steps rail (rule 4). Prep's and the Compendium's marks are 24 px with VT323 17 px numbers; the builder's are 26 px with 16 px numbers, and Level up's 22 px (24 when current) with 14 px.

Fix: One mark: 24 px, its number VT323 17 px.

Saved with and without its lamp

F3, the Atlas (Editing a pin); F, time and tools (templates, calendar)

Readiness is a lamp and words (rule 19). Writing a page and the Compendium's editor say Saved with its cyan lamp; the Atlas's pin editor and time and tools' templates and calendar write it as muted words.

The ruling card's violet rim

C2, C3, C3's running, C4 and C6, C5 (the GM panel's waiting cards)

GM-only is a tag, and a box carries no violet bar (rule 7). The card for a player asking the GM's ruling carries a 3 px violet rim; every other card that needs the GM carries the amber one. C3's values ask for both.

Eyebrows the fourth sweep missed

F, time and tools; F, story and people and F3 (downtime); C5 (calling for a roll)

The eyebrow is Bai Jamjuree 600, 11 px capitals at 0.12em (T 2.4), and the fourth sweep made it one style. Time and tools' field labels (Played on, Session) and its timeline's column heads (In the world, Day, The party) are still at 0.1em; the downtime's DAYS is 10.5 px and DAYS LEFT 12.5 px; the call for a roll's WAITING and success are at 0.1em.

Fix: The eyebrow for each, its colour kept where it carries a meaning.

The captures beside their pattern

Also checked, and matching: the fourth sweep's sixteen fixes hold (one notice, dialog and sheet titles at 20 px, title rows at 24 and 20 px, menu rows at 48 and 52 px, no phone row under 44 px, every switch one track, the GM ONLY tag one size). No text is clipped; the text past a phone frame belongs to strips that scroll sideways. Every line passes contrast in Dusk, and in Dawn every colour but the three in finding 2. Keyboard hints are one style, cards keep their edges, and the copy has no pronouns for characters, dashes, curly quotes or exclamation marks. Dawn draws 28,185 of 28,189 captures at the same size as Dusk.
